A chest X-ray showed a miliary pattern. The patient was diagnosed with histoplasmosis after lung biopsy and positive serology.
in_text_mentions: miliary pattern; multiple small (<3 mm) pulmonary nodules of similar size that are randomly distributed throughout both lungs. Hematogenous spread of the fungus from re-infection from a very recent (usually <3 days) substantial exposure results in multiple foci of inflammation distributed throughout the lung, without lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion [35]. The differential diagnosis is wide, including tuberculosis, aspergillosis and coccidioidomycosis. Spontaneous resolution over several weeks or gradual deterioration and death may follow, hence antifungal treatment is usually given (Fig 4).

panels.figure_caption: A. A 31-year-old woman with no comorbidities presented with facial plethora and oedema of the cervical region and upper limbs. A CT angiography scan revealed a lesion measuring 5.4 × 3.0 × 4.4 cm, with approximately 75% reduction in the caliber of the superior vena cava. She was diagnosed with pulmonary histoplasmosis after positive serology results obtained by two different methods. The mediastinal biopsy revealed only fibrosis. B. PET/CT scan showed a mediastinal mass with high glycolytic activity.
in_text_mentions: Fibrosing mediastinitis is a serious presentation associated with pulmonary histoplasmosis [16,18,35,87]. It is visualized as the accumulation of fibrotic tissue in the mediastinum structures, especially the middle mediastinum (Fig 6). This can lead to compression of various mediastinal structures such as the superior vena cava [31]. Fibrosing mediastinitis caused by H. capsulatum is the most common benign cause of superior vena cava syndrome [35]. The chest X-ray usually shows mediastinal widening [18,35,88].

panels.figure_caption: The present image from a histological section of the intestinal mucosa wrongly reported the presence of Leishmania amastigotes. The characteristic kinetoplasts of Leishmania, which typically exhibit stronger staining than the nucleus, are not observed in these oval structures. Under hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining at 100× magnification, the ovoid yeasts of H. capsulatum are visible. Yeasts measure 2 to 4 μm, have unstained cell walls with a distinct refractile capsule, and exhibit narrow-based budding. They are predominantly found phagocytosed within macrophages and histiocytes, often forming clusters of numerous organisms. Occasionally, they may also be observed in extracellular spaces [28].

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E-stained adrenal biopsy section showing small intracellular Histoplasma yeast forms with lucent halos clustered in macrophages; the textbook histologic presentation of adrenal histoplasmosis in this immunocompetent patient. B: Higher-magnification H&E adrenal biopsy section confirming intracellular Histoplasma yeast forms within macrophages; classic histology of adrenal histoplasmosis. C: PAS-stained adrenal biopsy section from a necrotic area showing spilled, haphazardly arranged Histoplasma yeast forms; consistent with necrotizing adrenal histoplasmosis. D: GMS-stained adrenal biopsy section from necrotic tissue demonstrating Histoplasma yeasts with narrow-based budding, a pathognomonic feature confirming adrenal histoplasmosis.

The article title further supports African histoplasmosis. B: Coronal FDG PET-CT demonstrates enlarged FDG-avid bilateral adrenal glands and hepatosplenomegaly, compatible with disseminated histoplasmosis. A: Wright-Giemsa bone marrow aspirate from the index solid-organ-transplant patient with confirmed disseminated histoplasmosis; multiple oval intracellular organisms within a histiocyte are the defining cytologic manifestation of Histoplasma capsulatum, and the disease-focused article title plus antigen confirmation support attribution. [raw subtype: disseminated] C: Bone marrow aspirate showing hemophagocytosis in the same confirmed histoplasmosis patient. Hemophagocytosis is a nonspecific reactive marrow finding that can accompany disseminated histoplasmosis but is not diagnostic of it, so it is recorded as a proposed finding with low-confidence disease attribution based on...

Peritoneal fluid was collected for culture; the media used included blood culture bottles and direct plating on Sabouraud dextrose agar, incubated for three weeks, the result was negative. Peritoneal fluid was collected for culture; the media used included blood culture bottles and direct plating on Sabouraud dextrose agar, incubated for three weeks, the result was negative. A segmental jejunal resection with jejunostomy was performed, and an omental biopsy was obtained for histopathological examination (figures 2 and 3). Both blood and peritoneal fluid cultures yielded negative results.

The omental biopsy revealed the presence of necrotizing caseous granulomas (figure 2). The frequency of granulomas was reported in 39.3% of HIV-positive patients reviewed in the literature by Assi et al. (2006) and in 44.4% of the patients evaluated in their study. However, patients with advanced cellular immunodeficiency may not present the typical characteristics of granulomatous inflammation and may not be observable 4. These granulomas are also common in peritoneal tuberculosis, but histologically, distinguishing them from gastrointestinal histoplasmosis is not possible 2.
